question: Will EU leaders at the 26–27 November 2026 Special European Council agree on additional EU financing for Ukraine's 2027 needs beyond the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: first European Council discussion of a large, contested, unanimity-requiring new Ukraine financing instrument — these are usually deferred (Oct 2025 reparations loan deferred to Dec; Dec 2025 €90bn agreed only at year-end with opt-outs). The Commission tables the ~€45bn new loan only on 18 Nov, eight days before the summit; reporting says the EU seeks a decision 'by end of year', pointing to 17–18 Dec; the issue is entangled with the MFF and Merz's all-27 demand, opposed by Fico, Babiš, Magyar and Bulgaria. Upside: the October EUCO mandate, strong German pressure, a floated opt-out template, and a low bar (agreement in principle with 'agree' wording counts). No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- Commission to present ~€45bn new loan for Ukraine 2027 (joint borrowing backed by EU budget headroom, mirroring the €90bn USL) to member states on 18 Nov 2026 (FT via UNN/Life.ru/Interia, 16 Nov 2026). Would cover ~2/3 of a ~€70bn 2027 gap; the rest would be sought from other partners.
- October 15-16 2026 EUCO tasked the Commission to prepare proposals to close the €70bn 2027 gap (Eurointegration, 9 Nov 2026).
- Dombrovskis, 9 Nov: preparing options for ~€45bn with all 27 contributing, 'cautiously optimistic'.
- Reports say the decision needs all 27; EU leaders will discuss at the 26-27 Nov summit, 'seeking to make a decision by the end of the year' (Eurointegration/serrarigroup, Nov 2026). The next EUCO is 17-18 Dec 2026.
- Merz ties German support for MFF 2028-34 to all members funding Ukraine and asked Costa to move the item earlier; Costa refused, kept it on 26-27 Nov, and allowed discussion at the Dublin informal summit on 13 Nov (Pravda/Yahoo, 11 Nov 2026).
- Opposition: Fico ('blackmail'; Slovakia won't join another loan), Hungarian PM Péter Magyar (against the MFF linkage), Babiš (letter to Costa: MFF can't depend on Ukraine financing); Bulgaria also seeks an exemption. Diplomats float an opt-out for HU/SK/CZ/BG (FT, 16 Nov).
- Precedent: Oct 2025 EUCO deferred the reparations loan; 18 Dec 2025 EUCO agreed the €90bn via joint borrowing with an HU/SK/CZ opt-out (Euronews/OSW, Dec 2025), i.e. agreement came at the second summit after initial discussion.
- The 26-27 Nov meeting is a Special EUCO also on the MFF; MFF deals historically take several summits.
- Costa/vdL joint statement 12 Nov: 'we will discuss Ukraine's urgent financing needs for 2027, based on the Commission's proposal' — wording is 'discuss', not 'decide'.
- Status quo: no new instrument agreed; the existing 2027 €45bn tranche (COM(2026)606) is decided by Ecofin and does not count.
- Resolves off the EUCO conclusions / Main results page (incl. any Ukraine text endorsed by a subset), requiring 'agree'/'decide' on new 2027 financing beyond the €90bn; 'call for', 'will revert' or 'invite further work' = NO.
- Event window: 26 Nov -> 27 Nov 2026 summit conclusions; as of 16 Nov, 0% elapsed.
- Searched for but not found: draft conclusions leaks, any prediction market (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, bookmakers: none), Costa's 13 Nov press remarks (page blocked).
calls.reference_class: European Council first-discussion summits on major new contested Ukraine financing instruments (2022-2025)

calls.reasoning: Base rate: when the Commission tables a major Ukraine financing proposal, EU leaders have often settled it at the decisive (usually December) summit, sometimes after one or more inconclusive meetings. Dec 2025 precedent: agreement in principle on a €90bn loan at the summit with three states not taking part. YES factors: the Commission tables a new €45bn budget-backed loan on 18 Nov; HU/SK/CZ/BG reportedly won't block and may get an opt-out (opt-outs count); Germany wanted it done sooner. NO factors: only 8 days between proposal and summit; Costa aims for year-end and Agence Europe says December is the target, with diplomats wanting it packaged with the MFF; Merz demands all 27 share the cost, which clashes with an opt-out; weak 'address' wording is a technical NO risk. No human market found (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, bookmakers checked).
calls.dossier:
- FT via Life.ru/Interia (16 Nov 2026): the Commission will present a new €45bn loan for Ukraine for 2027 to member states on Wed 18 Nov, backed by EU budget guarantees and joint borrowing, modelled on the €90bn loan; reported as needing unanimity; HU/SK/CZ/BG may be offered an opt-out.
- Euronews (16 Nov 2026): proposal expected Wednesday; covers two-thirds of the €70bn 2027 gap; EU budget guarantees it and covers the interest; frozen Russian assets not included; SK/HU/CZ/BG want to opt out.
- Hromadske (Nov 2026): Costa says 'normally we cover two thirds'; leaders aim to decide at the 26-27 Nov summit, otherwise continue on 17-18 Dec; a new joint-borrowing loan is the preferred option; HU/SK/CZ/BG won't participate but won't obstruct; Belgium rules out using the frozen assets; UK, Canada and Norway asked to contribute.
- Agence Europe (Nov 2026): Costa aims for agreement by year-end; December is the target for a final decision; a diplomat says it is 'logical to deal with these two issues [loan + MFF] together as part of an overall package'; frugal states may use the loan as leverage for cohesion cuts.
- Pravda (11 Nov 2026): Costa answered Merz's ultimatum by putting 2027 needs on the 26-27 Nov special summit, based on the Commission proposal.
- Background: Merz made support for the 2028-34 MFF conditional on all 27 sharing the cost of the 2027 gap; Czech PM Babiš wrote to Costa that the MFF cannot depend on Ukraine aid; Fico says Slovakia won't join another loan.
- Precedent: at the 18 Dec 2025 European Council, leaders agreed the €90bn loan in principle via enhanced cooperation, with HU/SK/CZ not participating; the Oct 2025 summit had used 'address financing needs' wording and deferred the decision.
- Status quo: no new instrument agreed; the 2027 €45bn tranche of the existing loan (COM(2026)606) is on a separate finance-minister track and does not count.
- Resolution: resolves off the 26-27 Nov conclusions/Ukraine text wording ('agree'/'decide' new financing, an amount, an instrument or an explicit commitment); 'call for', 'address', 'will revert' or 'invite work' count as NO.
- Event window: the 26-27 Nov 2026 summit only; as of 16 Nov, 0% elapsed (summit 10 days away).
- Searched but not found: draft conclusions text; any prediction market (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers).
calls.reference_class: Proposals for new EU Ukraine financing instruments: whether leaders agreed at the first summit after the proposal was tabled vs a later one (2022-2025: MFA+ 2022, Ukraine Facility Dec 2023->Feb 2024, €90bn loan Oct->Dec 2025)

calls.reasoning: The Commission tables a new ~€45bn EU-budget-backed loan on 18 Nov, only 8 days before the special summit. Costa's stated goal is a political deal by year-end, with the 17-18 Dec European Council as the explicit fallback. The Dec 2025 precedent shows agreement in principle with opt-outs via enhanced cooperation is feasible about two weeks after a proposal. Counter-forces: Merz demands all-27 participation and links it to the MFF, which Czechia and Hungary reject; Slovakia, Hungary, Czechia and Bulgaria seek exemptions; and a special MFF summit risks ending without conclusions. Leaders may only 'take note' or 'revert' in December. No human prediction market found.
calls.dossier:
- Commission (Dombrovskis, 9 Nov 2026; Eurointegration, Kyiv Independent) is preparing a new ~€45bn loan for 2027 on top of the €90bn Ukraine Support Loan. Per the FT (via Life.ru and Interia, 16 Nov), it is joint borrowing guaranteed by the EU budget and will be presented to member states on Wed 18 Nov 2026.
- Ukraine's residual 2027 gap is ~€70bn; the EU aims to cover about two-thirds (~€46.7bn) (Hromadske; Brussels Signal Oct 2026). The October 2026 European Council tasked the Commission with producing proposals.
- Costa refused Merz's request to fast-track; the item stays on the 26-27 Nov special EUCO alongside the MFF 2028-34. Fallback: if there is no agreement, retry on 17-18 Dec (Censor.net, Nov 2026). The Commission/Costa aim for a political deal by year-end (Brussels Signal, Oct 2026).
- Joint Costa/von der Leyen statement, 12 Nov: leaders 'will discuss' 2027 needs 'based on the Commission's proposal' at the 26-27 Nov EUCO.
- Opposition: Fico says Slovakia won't participate in another loan; Hungary opposes the MFF linkage; Babiš wrote to Costa that the MFF cannot depend on Ukraine support; Bulgaria (Radev) is expected to opt out. CZ/HU/SK opted out of the €90bn loan via enhanced cooperation. Diplomats say an opt-out may be offered again (Sputnik/Kyiv Independent, 12 Nov).
- Merz threatens to block or condition the MFF unless all member states back joint Ukraine funding (Le Monde, 11 Nov). This creates tension with the opt-out solution.
- Open issues per diplomats: participation (all 27 vs opt-outs) and how to fund interest costs (Kyiv Independent).
- Precedent: Dec 2025 EUCO agreed the €90bn loan in principle with opt-outs about two weeks after the Commission's early-Dec proposals, after the Oct 2025 EUCO deferred. Precedent: the Feb 2020 special MFF EUCO ended with no agreement or conclusions.
- Only ~€20bn of the €90bn had been disbursed as of Oct 2026 (Brussels Signal).
- Status quo: no new EU instrument for 2027 is agreed yet; the 2027 tranche of the €90bn (COM(2026)606) does not count.
- Resolves off the EUCO 26-27 Nov conclusions/main results or a separate Ukraine text (a subset of leaders is OK) using 'agree/decide' wording on new 2027 financing. Mere 'discuss/invite/revert' = NO.
- Event window: 26-27 Nov 2026 meeting; as of 16 Nov 2026 the meeting is 10 days away.
- Searched, not found: any Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market; draft conclusions text; diplomat statements on whether 26-27 Nov or 17-18 Dec is the realistic decision date.
calls.reference_class: EU special/regular summits where a major new Ukraine financing instrument was proposed shortly before (Dec 2023/Feb 2024 Ukraine Facility; Oct 2025/Dec 2025 reparations/€90bn loan): first-scheduled summit agreement rate

calls.reasoning: Base rate: the first European Council discussion of a large new Ukraine financing instrument that needs unanimity usually ends in deferral (reparations loan in Oct 2025 → Dec 2025 deal). The Commission tables the ~€45bn new loan only on 18 Nov, 8 days before the summit. It is designed with all 27 participating while SK/HU/CZ/BG want to opt out, and diplomats frame it as a package with the MFF, which will not close at this special summit. Reporting is mixed: some says leaders expect to decide on 26-27 Nov, other reports say 'by end of year', with 17-18 Dec as the explicit fallback. Upside: a low bar (agreement in principle with opt-outs counts), German pressure for speed, and the Dec 2025 opt-out template. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: The main dispute was whether 26-27 Nov or 17-18 Dec is the decision point. My searches turned up both framings: Hromadske and Censor say leaders expect to decide on 26-27 Nov with Dec as fallback, while Euronews (16 Nov), the FT-based reports and Brussels Signal say 'by the end of the year'. That leaves this a judgment call. I confirmed the new loan proposal is only due on 18 Nov and is designed around all 27, with four states wanting out. Fico repeated his refusal on 15 Nov. The Dublin informal summit settled the peace-talks delegation, not the money. I found no leaked draft conclusions and no prediction market. On the judgment, I weight the short timeline, the unresolved opt-out-vs-all-27 clash and the MFF package logic above the low resolution bar, which puts me near Run 3.

disagreements.claim: Leaders aim to decide at 26-27 Nov rather than in December
disagreements.verdict: Mixed: sources show both Nov-as-target-with-Dec-fallback and 'by end of year' framings; not settled
Confirmed: due 18 Nov, 8 days before the summit

disagreements.claim: Opt-out for SK/HU/CZ/BG will be accepted, enabling an agreement
disagreements.verdict: Unresolved; the all-27 design and Merz's stance cut against a quick opt-out deal

disagreements.claim: Linkage to the MFF delays the Ukraine deal to a package decision
disagreements.verdict: Plausible per diplomats; weighted toward NO
